errors.text: The generated hypothesis substitutes the CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy for the targeted dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy.

It identifies finite-temperature magnetic moments, phase stability, and stacking-fault energy as the improvement target, whereas the target property is coercivity, specifically exceeding the approximately 100 Oe limit of single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys.
It omits the C14 Laves phase, fcc/C14 coexistence, chemical segregation, and the comparison with the C14-dominant Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 alloy.

Its longitudinal-spin-fluctuation mechanism is unrelated to the target mechanism involving antiferromagnetic coupling to Ti, spin canting, orbital-moment-assisted domain-wall pinning, and dual-phase interfaces.
The cited evidence supports longitudinal spin fluctuations in paramagnetic CoCrFeMnNi but does not support the asserted scientific gap concerning orbital moments.
